/-!
# Conjecture 7.45

by D. M. Smirnov

Does the $Q$-theory of the class of all finite groups (in the sense of 2.40) coincide with
the $Q$-theory of a single finitely presented group?

Following Mal'cev (Problem 2.40 of the notebook), a *quasi-identity* in the language of
groups is a universal Horn sentence
$$\forall x_1 \dots x_n \;
  \bigl(u_1(\bar x) = v_1(\bar x) \wedge \dots \wedge u_m(\bar x) = v_m(\bar x)
  \;\to\; u(\bar x) = v(\bar x)\bigr),$$
where $m \ge 0$ and $u_1, v_1, \dots, u_m, v_m, u, v$ are group words in the finitely many
variables $x_1, \dots, x_n$ (identities are the quasi-identities with $m = 0$).
The $Q$-theory of a class $\mathfrak{K}$ of groups is the set of all quasi-identities that
are true in every group of $\mathfrak{K}$; the $Q$-theory of a single group $G$ is the
$Q$-theory of the class $\{G\}$.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

blocks.code:
structure GroupQuasiIdentity where
  /-- The number $n$ of variables. -/
  numVars : ℕ
  /-- The premises $u_1 = v_1, \dots, u_m = v_m$, as pairs of group words. -/
  premises : List (FreeGroup (Fin numVars) × FreeGroup (Fin numVars))
  /-- The conclusion $u = v$, as a pair of group words. -/
  conclusion : FreeGroup (Fin numVars) × FreeGroup (Fin numVars)
blocks.docstring:
A quasi-identity in the language of groups, in the variables $x_0, \dots, x_{n-1}$:
$$\forall \bar x \;
  \bigl(u_1(\bar x) = v_1(\bar x) \wedge \dots \wedge u_m(\bar x) = v_m(\bar x)
  \;\to\; u(\bar x) = v(\bar x)\bigr).$$
The group words $u_i, v_i, u, v$ are recorded as elements of the free group on `Fin n`;
two group words define the same element of the free group exactly when they take the same
value in every group, so this loses nothing. The list of premises may be empty, in which
case the quasi-identity is an identity.

justification.closest_existing_considered: FirstOrder.Language / FirstOrder.Language.BoundedFormula (Mathlib.ModelTheory): only ring and field languages exist (Language.ring), no group language and no Horn-formula predicate; FreeGroup (used as the term algebra).
justification.name: Kourovka.«7.45».GroupQuasiIdentity
justification.why_needed: Mathlib has no first-order language of groups and no notion of quasi-identity (universal Horn sentence). The structure records the number of variables, a finite list of premise equations and a conclusion equation between elements of FreeGroup (Fin n).

blocks.name: GroupQuasiIdentity
blocks.text:
/--
A quasi-identity in the language of groups, in the variables $x_0, \dots, x_{n-1}$:
$$\forall \bar x \;
  \bigl(u_1(\bar x) = v_1(\bar x) \wedge \dots \wedge u_m(\bar x) = v_m(\bar x)
  \;\to\; u(\bar x) = v(\bar x)\bigr).$$
The group words $u_i, v_i, u, v$ are recorded as elements of the free group on `Fin n`;
two group words define the same element of the free group exactly when they take the same
value in every group, so this loses nothing. The list of premises may be empty, in which
case the quasi-identity is an identity.
-/
structure GroupQuasiIdentity where
  /-- The number $n$ of variables. -/
  numVars : ℕ
  /-- The premises $u_1 = v_1, \dots, u_m = v_m$, as pairs of group words. -/
  premises : List (FreeGroup (Fin numVars) × FreeGroup (Fin numVars))
  /-- The conclusion $u = v$, as a pair of group words. -/
  conclusion : FreeGroup (Fin numVars) × FreeGroup (Fin numVars)

blocks.code:
def GroupQuasiIdentity.Holds (q : GroupQuasiIdentity) (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ x : Fin q.numVars → G,
    (∀ p ∈ q.premises, FreeGroup.lift x p.1 = FreeGroup.lift x p.2) →
      FreeGroup.lift x q.conclusion.1 = FreeGroup.lift x q.conclusion.2
blocks.docstring:
A quasi-identity $\forall \bar x\,(\bigwedge_i u_i(\bar x) = v_i(\bar x) \to u(\bar x) = v(\bar x))$
holds in a group $G$ if for every assignment $\bar x$ of values in $G$ to the variables,
$u(\bar x) = v(\bar x)$ whenever $u_i(\bar x) = v_i(\bar x)$ for all $i$.

justification.closest_existing_considered: FirstOrder.Language.Sentence.Realize / Theory.Model (not applicable without a group language); FreeGroup.lift.
justification.name: Kourovka.«7.45».GroupQuasiIdentity.Holds
justification.why_needed: Satisfaction of a quasi-identity in a group: for every assignment of the variables, if all premise equations hold then the conclusion holds. Evaluation of words via FreeGroup.lift.

blocks.name: GroupQuasiIdentity.Holds
blocks.text:
/--
A quasi-identity $\forall \bar x\,(\bigwedge_i u_i(\bar x) = v_i(\bar x) \to u(\bar x) = v(\bar x))$
holds in a group $G$ if for every assignment $\bar x$ of values in $G$ to the variables,
$u(\bar x) = v(\bar x)$ whenever $u_i(\bar x) = v_i(\bar x)$ for all $i$.
-/
def GroupQuasiIdentity.Holds (q : GroupQuasiIdentity) (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ x : Fin q.numVars → G,
    (∀ p ∈ q.premises, FreeGroup.lift x p.1 = FreeGroup.lift x p.2) →
      FreeGroup.lift x q.conclusion.1 = FreeGroup.lift x q.conclusion.2

blocks.code:
def qTheory (G : Type*) [Group G] : Set GroupQuasiIdentity :=
  {q | q.Holds G}
blocks.docstring: The $Q$-theory of a group $G$: the set of all quasi-identities that hold in $G$.

justification.closest_existing_considered: FirstOrder.Language.completeTheory (first-order theory of a structure; not restricted to quasi-identities and no group language).
justification.name: Kourovka.«7.45».qTheory
justification.why_needed: The Q-theory of a single group: the set of quasi-identities holding in it.

blocks.name: qTheory

blocks.code:
def qTheoryFiniteGroups : Set GroupQuasiIdentity :=
  {q | ∀ (H : Type) [Group H] [Finite H], q.Holds H}
blocks.docstring:
The $Q$-theory of the class of all finite groups: the set of all quasi-identities that hold
in every finite group, i.e. the intersection of the $Q$-theories of all finite groups.

justification.closest_existing_considered: None in Mathlib or FormalConjecturesForMathlib (no quasivariety/Q-theory notion).
justification.name: Kourovka.«7.45».qTheoryFiniteGroups
justification.why_needed: The Q-theory of the class of all finite groups: quasi-identities true in every finite group (H : Type, [Group H], [Finite H]).

blocks.name: qTheoryFiniteGroups

blocks.docstring:
A group is finitely presented if it is isomorphic to a group given by finitely many
generators and finitely many defining relations.

justification.name: Kourovka.«7.45».IsFinitelyPresented
justification.why_needed: Mathlib has finitely presented algebras/modules (Algebra.FinitePresentation, Module.FinitePresentation) and finitely generated groups (Group.FG) but no finitely presented groups. Defined as isomorphic to PresentedGroup rels with finitely many generators Fin n and a finite set of relations.

blocks.name: IsFinitelyPresented
blocks.text:
/--
A group is finitely presented if it is isomorphic to a group given by finitely many
generators and finitely many defining relations.
-/
def IsFinitelyPresented (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∃ (n : ℕ) (rels : Set (FreeGroup (Fin n))),
    rels.Finite ∧ Nonempty (G ≃* PresentedGroup rels)

blocks.code:
@[category research open, AMS 3 20]
theorem kourovka.«7.45» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∃ (G : Type) (_ : Group G), IsFinitelyPresented G ∧ qTheory G = qTheoryFiniteGroups := by
  sorry
blocks.docstring:
Does the $Q$-theory of the class of all finite groups (in the sense of 2.40) coincide with
the $Q$-theory of a single finitely presented group?

That is: is there a finitely presented group $G$ such that a quasi-identity holds in $G$ if
and only if it holds in every finite group?

  numVars := 1
  premises := [(FreeGroup.of 0 ^ 2, 1)]
  conclusion := (FreeGroup.of 0, 1)

justification.name: Kourovka.«7.45».squareQuasiIdentity

blocks.name: squareQuasiIdentity
blocks.text:

blocks.code:
@[category test, AMS 3 20]
theorem squareQuasiIdentity_not_mem_qTheoryFiniteGroups :
    squareQuasiIdentity ∉ qTheoryFiniteGroups := by
  intro h
  have := h (Multiplicative (ZMod 2)) (fun _ => Multiplicative.ofAdd 1)
  simp [squareQuasiIdentity] at this
  exact this (by decide)

claims.decomposer_note: Single yes/no question with an implicit existential quantifier: is there a finitely presented group G (finitely many generators and relations) such that the set of quasi-identities (Mal'cev's Q-theory from Kourovka 2.40: universal Horn sentences ∀x̄ (⋀ᵢ uᵢ(x̄)=vᵢ(x̄) → u(x̄)=v(x̄)) in the language of groups, with n ≥ 0 premises so identities are included) true in G is exactly the set of quasi-identities true in every finite group — equivalently, G generates the same quasivariety as the class of all finite groups; quasi-identities must be formalized with finitely many variables and finitely many premises, and the Q-theory of the class is the intersection over all finite groups.
claims.reviewer_why: All eight candidates are mathematically equivalent and faithful: quasi-identities with finitely many variables (Fin n) and finitely many (possibly zero) premises, words encoded in FreeGroup (Fin n) and evaluated by FreeGroup.lift (loses nothing since free-group equality = equality of terms in every group), the Q-theory of the class of finite groups as the intersection over all `(G : Type) [Group G] [Finite G]`, finitely presented = isomorphic to `PresentedGroup rels` on Fin n generators with finitely many relators, and `answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ G, finitely presented ∧ qTheory G = qTheory(finite groups)` so answer(True) is the positive answer. c03 was chosen because it states 'coincide' literally as set equality of named Q-theories, defines finite presentability as a predicate on an abstract group (closest to 'a single finitely presented group'), and includes the most useful @[category test] lemmas for the bespoke definitions (including the quasi-identity x^2=1 → x=1, which fails in Z/2 but holds in Z, exercising exactly the finite-vs-infinite distinction at the heart of the problem). Used verbatim; compiles with only the sorry warning.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 7.45

by D. M. Smirnov

Does the $Q$-theory of the class of all finite groups (in the sense of 2.40) coincide with
the $Q$-theory of a single finitely presented group?

Following Mal'cev (Problem 2.40 of the notebook), a *quasi-identity* in the language of
groups is a universal Horn sentence
$$\forall x_1 \dots x_n \;
  \bigl(u_1(\bar x) = v_1(\bar x) \wedge \dots \wedge u_m(\bar x) = v_m(\bar x)
  \;\to\; u(\bar x) = v(\bar x)\bigr),$$
where $m \ge 0$ and $u_1, v_1, \dots, u_m, v_m, u, v$ are group words in the finitely many
variables $x_1, \dots, x_n$ (identities are the quasi-identities with $m = 0$).
The $Q$-theory of a class $\mathfrak{K}$ of groups is the set of all quasi-identities that
are true in every group of $\mathfrak{K}$; the $Q$-theory of a single group $G$ is the
$Q$-theory of the class $\{G\}$.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«7.45»

/--
A quasi-identity in the language of groups, in the variables $x_0, \dots, x_{n-1}$:
$$\forall \bar x \;
  \bigl(u_1(\bar x) = v_1(\bar x) \wedge \dots \wedge u_m(\bar x) = v_m(\bar x)
  \;\to\; u(\bar x) = v(\bar x)\bigr).$$
The group words $u_i, v_i, u, v$ are recorded as elements of the free group on `Fin n`;
two group words define the same element of the free group exactly when they take the same
value in every group, so this loses nothing. The list of premises may be empty, in which
case the quasi-identity is an identity.
-/
structure GroupQuasiIdentity where
  /-- The number $n$ of variables. -/
  numVars : ℕ
  /-- The premises $u_1 = v_1, \dots, u_m = v_m$, as pairs of group words. -/
  premises : List (FreeGroup (Fin numVars) × FreeGroup (Fin numVars))
  /-- The conclusion $u = v$, as a pair of group words. -/
  conclusion : FreeGroup (Fin numVars) × FreeGroup (Fin numVars)

/--
A quasi-identity $\forall \bar x\,(\bigwedge_i u_i(\bar x) = v_i(\bar x) \to u(\bar x) = v(\bar x))$
holds in a group $G$ if for every assignment $\bar x$ of values in $G$ to the variables,
$u(\bar x) = v(\bar x)$ whenever $u_i(\bar x) = v_i(\bar x)$ for all $i$.
-/
def GroupQuasiIdentity.Holds (q : GroupQuasiIdentity) (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ x : Fin q.numVars → G,
    (∀ p ∈ q.premises, FreeGroup.lift x p.1 = FreeGroup.lift x p.2) →
      FreeGroup.lift x q.conclusion.1 = FreeGroup.lift x q.conclusion.2

/-- The $Q$-theory of a group $G$: the set of all quasi-identities that hold in $G$. -/
def qTheory (G : Type*) [Group G] : Set GroupQuasiIdentity :=
  {q | q.Holds G}

/--
The $Q$-theory of the class of all finite groups: the set of all quasi-identities that hold
in every finite group, i.e. the intersection of the $Q$-theories of all finite groups.
-/
def qTheoryFiniteGroups : Set GroupQuasiIdentity :=
  {q | ∀ (H : Type) [Group H] [Finite H], q.Holds H}

/--
A group is finitely presented if it is isomorphic to a group given by finitely many
generators and finitely many defining relations.
-/
def IsFinitelyPresented (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∃ (n : ℕ) (rels : Set (FreeGroup (Fin n))),
    rels.Finite ∧ Nonempty (G ≃* PresentedGroup rels)

/--
Does the $Q$-theory of the class of all finite groups (in the sense of 2.40) coincide with
the $Q$-theory of a single finitely presented group?

That is: is there a finitely presented group $G$ such that a quasi-identity holds in $G$ if
and only if it holds in every finite group?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 3 20]
theorem kourovka.«7.45» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∃ (G : Type) (_ : Group G), IsFinitelyPresented G ∧ qTheory G = qTheoryFiniteGroups := by
  sorry

/-- Every quasi-identity holds in the trivial group. -/
@[category test, AMS 3 20]
theorem GroupQuasiIdentity.holds_unit (q : GroupQuasiIdentity) : q.Holds Unit :=
  fun _ _ => Subsingleton.elim _ _

/-- The $Q$-theory of the class of all finite groups is contained in the $Q$-theory of each
finite group. -/
@[category test, AMS 3 20]
theorem qTheoryFiniteGroups_subset_qTheory (H : Type) [Group H] [Finite H] :
    qTheoryFiniteGroups ⊆ qTheory H :=
  fun _ hq => hq H

/-- A group given by finitely many generators and relations is finitely presented. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem isFinitelyPresented_presentedGroup {n : ℕ} (rels : Set (FreeGroup (Fin n)))
    (h : rels.Finite) : IsFinitelyPresented (PresentedGroup rels) :=
  ⟨n, rels, h, ⟨MulEquiv.refl _⟩⟩

/-- The quasi-identity $\forall x\,(x^2 = 1 \to x = 1)$. -/
def squareQuasiIdentity : GroupQuasiIdentity where
  numVars := 1
  premises := [(FreeGroup.of 0 ^ 2, 1)]
  conclusion := (FreeGroup.of 0, 1)

/-- The quasi-identity $\forall x\,(x^2 = 1 \to x = 1)$ fails in the group of order two, so it
does not belong to the $Q$-theory of the class of all finite groups. -/
@[category test, AMS 3 20]
theorem squareQuasiIdentity_not_mem_qTheoryFiniteGroups :
    squareQuasiIdentity ∉ qTheoryFiniteGroups := by
  intro h
  have := h (Multiplicative (ZMod 2)) (fun _ => Multiplicative.ofAdd 1)
  simp [squareQuasiIdentity] at this
  exact this (by decide)

/-- The quasi-identity $\forall x\,(x^2 = 1 \to x = 1)$ holds in the infinite cyclic group. -/
@[category test, AMS 3 20]
theorem squareQuasiIdentity_holds_int : squareQuasiIdentity.Holds (Multiplicative ℤ) := by
  intro x hx
  simpa [squareQuasiIdentity] using hx

end Kourovka.«7.45»

items: Group terms are encoded as elements of FreeGroup (Fin n) rather than as syntactic terms in a first-order language of groups. Two group terms give the same free-group element iff they agree in every group, and every free-group element is represented by a term, so a quasi-identity holds in G iff its free-group encoding does; the equality of Q-theories is therefore unaffected.

Premises are a List (possibly empty), so identities count as quasi-identities (n ≥ 0 premises, as in the decomposition notes). If one insists on n ≥ 1 premises the question is equivalent, since an identity u = v holds in G iff the quasi-identity (x = x → u = v) does.

Finite groups are quantified over H : Type (with [Group H] [Finite H]); the finitely presented group G also lives in Type. Every finite group and every finitely presented group is isomorphic to one in Type 0, and satisfaction of quasi-identities is invariant under isomorphism, so nothing is lost.

IsFinitelyPresented G is defined as ∃ n, ∃ rels : Set (FreeGroup (Fin n)), rels.Finite ∧ Nonempty (G ≃* PresentedGroup rels), i.e. finitely many generators and finitely many defining relations, up to isomorphism.
The Q-theory of the class is stated as set equality with the Q-theory of the single group ('coincide'). The docstring explains the 2.40 sense of Q-theory (Mal'cev's quasi-identities).
AMS tags 3 (mathematical logic: quasi-identities/universal Horn theories) and 20 (group theory).

Added a few @[category test] lemmas with short proofs to sanity-check the bespoke definitions (trivial group satisfies everything; x^2 = 1 → x = 1 fails for finite groups but holds in ℤ; PresentedGroup of a finite presentation is finitely presented).

reviewer_notes: Statement read with the implicit existential: does there exist a finitely presented group whose set of true quasi-identities equals the set of quasi-identities true in every finite group. 'Q-theory in the sense of 2.40' = Mal'cev's quasi-identity theory; premises count n ≥ 0 was allowed (identities included) — this does not affect the question since an identity u=v is equivalent to the quasi-identity x=x → u=v, so equality of the n≥0 theories and of the n≥1 theories are equivalent. Groups quantified in universe Type; finite and finitely presented groups are all isomorphic to groups in Type and satisfaction of quasi-identities is isomorphism-invariant. The bespoke definitions (GroupQuasiIdentity, Holds, qTheory, qTheoryFiniteGroups, IsFinitelyPresented) are generic and could be moved to FormalConjecturesForMathlib by a maintainer; they were kept in the problem file since only one file is produced. No candidate omitted the slot; all reports' modeling decisions are consistent with each other and with the source.
